1 · Intro

When to use it.

Signed letters and approvals belong in the employee's personnel file in Oracle, as document records. A document record is the file plus details about it: its type, name, and the dates it covers.

Use the right type, name, and dates so the record can be found later.

Use this whenYou have a final, signed document to file: discipline, a compensation letter, a performance review, or a leave or accommodation approval.

2 · Walk through

Step by step.

Follow along in Oracle HCM. Check off each step as you go.

Types, names, and dates
Document TypeUse for, names, and dates
Performance and DisciplineWritten, Final, or Termination level (Discipline or PACP). Names like "Written Warning - Discipline". Discipline: To Date is 12 months after the From Date. PACP: To Date is the end of the plan (for example, 90 days).
Compensation LettersAnnual increase, bonus, interim pay, and salary increase letters (equity, market, reclass). Use From and To Date for interim or time-limited pay.
Performance ReviewAny review or goal-setting document. Names like "Performance Review - (review dates)". From and To Date = the period reviewed.
Leave and Accommodation DocumentationApproval letters for FMLA, Non-FMLA, State Leave, Personal Leave, and Accommodation. From and To Date = the approved timeframe.

Watch-outs

  • Attach only the final signed copy.
  • Questions about which type to use go to your HR Consultant.
  • Confirm the exact Document Records menu path in Vanderbilt's Oracle during a recorded demo.

HCM Academy job aid · Document Records & Reporting

Add a document record

Use when: You have a final, signed document to file: discipline, a compensation letter, a performance review, or a leave or accommodation approval. · System: Oracle HCM (Document Records)

  1. Open Document Records for the employee.
  2. Click Add.
  3. Document Type: pick the type that matches.
  4. Name: use the naming convention shown in the description.
  5. Issued On: the date the document was presented to the employee.
  6. From Date and To Date: the period the document covers.
  7. Leave Issuing Comments and Context Value blank.
  8. Attach the final signed copy and click Submit.
